title: CYBRIK Suite W2-I transport binding — PROPOSED delta against the ACCEPTED W2-D inference packet manifest
description: PROPOSED, UNAPPLIED delta record for the W2-I inference-plane transport binding. Under the recorded Founder decision (Option A, 2026-07-26) the accepted W2-D packet is the SOLE owner of the four inference operations, so the transport binding enters ONLY as a compatible successor revision of the W2-D-owned OpenAPI member — never as a second plane, a second path owner, or a second compatibility manifest. This file is the single declaration site for that candidate: it pins the accepted upstream bytes it was reviewed against, pins the candidate bytes it proposes to add, discloses the compatibility consequences honestly, and enumerates the changes that a FUTURE, separately recorded Gate W2-I status flip would apply to the accepted W2-D manifest. It applies none of them now. It is not acceptance, not implementation authorization, not a stable v1/GA promotion, not an immutable bundle tag, and it declares no operational endpoint, deployment, credential, or runtime evidence.
x-cybrik-manifest-self-denial: This artifact is NOT a compatibility manifest and must never be read, indexed, released, or renamed as one. It carries no packet identity of its own: the only compatibility manifest that governs these operations is the ACCEPTED W2-D packet manifest named in proposed_manifest_changes.target_manifest. The filename deliberately does not end in '.manifest.json'. A second manifest covering the same operations is precisely the shape Founder Option A rejected (G-W2I-2).
x-cybrik-applies-at: APPLY-ONLY-AT a future Gate W2-I status flip that is explicitly recorded by the Founder with evidence (ADR-0001 D5). Until that flip exists, every proposed_* block in this file is a description of an intended change and has no effect on any accepted byte.
x-cybrik-grants: NO ACCEPTANCE AUTHORITY, NO RUNTIME AUTHORITY, NO ENDPOINT AUTHORITY. This delta cannot accept a contract, authorize an implementation, certify a runtime, declare a deployment, or open Gate W2-I. Conformance-validator success against these bytes is evidence of internal consistency only.
wire_scope: NO SERVER / NO ENDPOINT (G-W2I-5). The candidate successor OpenAPI member is mapping notes only: it declares no servers block, operational host, deployment URL, credential, key, or secret. Deployment and credentials remain product-owned.
mcp_scope: OUT OF SCOPE. MCP is a Tool/Agent gateway adapter and NOT the inference trust boundary. This candidate neither defines an MCP server/tool/action contract nor grants tool/function/agent authority.

compatibility_disclosure.basis: ADR-0001 D2 — pre-GA revisions may move quickly, but EVERY incompatibility must be explicit in the compatibility record. No silent breakage, ever.
compatibility_disclosure.namespace: Disjoint cybrik.transport-* schema identifiers plus one successor revision of an existing W2-D-owned OpenAPI member. No accepted schema identifier, event type, or channel is redefined.
compatibility_disclosure.change_classification: COMPATIBLE SUCCESSOR REVISION WITH DISCLOSED CONSUMER-VISIBLE TIGHTENING. Every operation-level interface element the accepted predecessor declares is preserved exactly; the changes are an authorization tightening and an error-surface widening, both disclosed below. Under a strict pre-GA reading this is a MINOR revision (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0) because no declared interface element is removed or renamed; it is NOT claimed to be purely additive.
preserved_exactly: The four (method, path) pairs: GET /api/v1/model-classes, GET /api/v1/model-classes/{model_class}/health, POST /api/v1/inferences, POST /api/v1/summarizations — same set, no addition, no removal.

All four operationIds verbatim: listModelClasses, getModelClassHealth, createInference, createAlertSummarization. No suffix, no rename; a client generated against the accepted predecessor keeps its method names.

Every operation-level parameters list byte-for-byte, including the mandatory Idempotency-Key and the traceparent header on the two creates and the model_class path parameter on the health read. The two new headers are OPTIONAL and are declared at PATH-ITEM level precisely so no operation's own parameters list changes.
Every requestBody, including its required flag and its accepted request-schema binding, on both creates.
Every 200 response binding, including the accepted result and capability/health schemas.

The accepted provider-neutral ModelInferenceError shape on 422 and 503 of both creates: it is retained as one branch of a two-branch oneOf, never replaced and never dropped, so a client generated against the predecessor still deserializes a conformant body on every status the predecessor binds.
breaking_changes: AUTHORIZATION TIGHTENING (consumer-visible): every operation now AND-requires mutual TLS workload identity plus a certificate-bound at+jwt delegation token in a SINGLE security requirement object. A consumer that presents neither, or only one of the two, is refused fail-closed where the predecessor document declared no security requirement at all. This is a machine-readable restatement of the transport security the ACCEPTED W2-D mapping notes already state in prose and that the accepted W2-F profile already requires on this seam — it grants no new tool, model, approval, agent, or execution authority to anyone, and it removes no capability from an already-conformant caller. It is disclosed as a break because the predecessor document was silent in machine-readable form and a generated client may not have been built to present both layers.

ERROR-SURFACE WIDENING on the two creates: 400, 401, 403, 409 and 429 are now declared where the predecessor declared only 422 and 503. A generated client with a closed response map may encounter a status it did not model. No previously declared status is removed and no 5xx beyond 503 is exposed.
ERROR-SURFACE WIDENING on the two reads: 401, 403, 429 and 503 are now declared where the predecessor declared only 200. Same consequence and same bound.

RESPONSE-SHAPE WIDENING on 422 and 503 of both creates: the body becomes a two-branch oneOf, so a consumer that deserialized those statuses STRICTLY into the accepted ModelInferenceError may now receive a typed transport/authorization error instead. The accepted branch is retained unmodified and the two branches are disjoint; a consumer that discriminates on the branch is unaffected.
non_breaking_additions: Two OPTIONAL headers declared at path-item level — the predecessor's traceparent extended to the reads, and an optional caller deadline. A client that sends neither behaves exactly as it does against the predecessor.
A neutral x-cybrik-operation-token per operation, recorded in the closed operation_registry below.
compatibility_disclosure.authority_boundary: The AND-required mTLS plus certificate-bound delegation binding is an authorization TIGHTENING of an accepted prose requirement into machine-readable form. It creates NO tool, function, agent, capability, approval, execution, model-selection, or runtime authority; it declares no server and no endpoint; model output remains untrusted data and is never an authorization, approval, or action trigger.

trust_invariants.note: Fail-closed invariants evaluated for the candidate, preserved unchanged from the candidate's earlier review. Structural TT-* rules are encoded by schemas and negative fixtures; runtime-only TX-* rules require relying-party enforcement. Validator success is conformance evidence only and cannot accept this candidate.
structural: TT-1 mTLS-bound REST/JSON: mutual_tls is required true and rest/json is the compatibility authority; bearer-only transport is inexpressible.
TT-2 no forwarded end-user token: the advisory body is closed and cannot carry an end-user credential or static bearer.
TT-3 no model, vendor, tool or agent authority: transport and advisory objects are closed and cannot grant execution authority.

TT-4 replay control: a create presentation (rest_binding.method POST with requires_idempotency_key true) structurally requires a root idempotency_key of at least 16 characters, and the method and idempotency policy must agree, so a create cannot declare itself exempt and a safe read that declares no key is never forced to carry one.
TT-5 safe retry only: retriable operations must be safe or idempotency-guarded.
TT-6 asymmetric-only delegation: the accepted W2-F token is composed by reference and excludes shared-secret or unsecured algorithms.
TT-7 fail-closed denial: every transport authorization error requires fail_closed true.
TT-8 closed error surface: only typed 400, 401, 403, 409, 422, 429 and 503 statuses are expressible; no 500 is exposed.
TT-9 no secret leak: typed errors are closed and require an audited decision_id without carrying token, credential or key material.
runtime_only: TX-1 proof-of-possession: the observed mTLS peer-certificate thumbprint must equal the delegation token cnf x5t#S256 binding.
TX-2 audience binding: token audience must exactly equal the relying party audience.
TX-3 tenant binding: advisory tenant must equal the authoritative token tenant.
TX-4 operation binding: advisory, token and REST operation names must match.
TX-5 marking non-escalation: advisory data marking must not exceed the token ceiling.
TX-6 org-scope binding: an advisory org scope, when present, must equal the token org scope and grants no authority by itself.
TX-7 replay rejection: a second presentation of an already-seen token jti and idempotency-key pair must be rejected.
TX-8 feature flag default-off: a disabled operation must apply its fail-closed disabled behavior and cannot be silently permitted.
trust_invariants.runtime_evaluation_order: The relying party evaluates the runtime rules in this fixed fail-closed order: TX-1 proof-of-possession, TX-2 audience, issuer pinning, TX-3 tenant, TX-4 operation, TX-5 marking, TX-6 org scope, TX-8 feature flag, TX-7 replay. TX-8 precedes TX-7 deliberately: an operation whose feature flag is disabled must be refused before the replay and idempotency cache is consulted, because a disabled operation is never admitted to that cache and a replay verdict on it would be a fiction. Both outcomes are rejections, so the order decides which typed rule is returned, never whether the call is denied. A single presentation can violate several rules at once, and every negative-semantic fixture in this candidate deliberately reuses the canonical token jti and idempotency key; each such fixture therefore declares the primary rule it exists to witness, and the validator requires the relying party to return exactly that rule. Truthiness alone would let TX-7 shadow TX-8 and leave the feature-flag rule vacuous.
trust_invariants.non_vacuity: Every structural TT rule is witnessed by at least one declared negative-schema fixture, and every runtime TX rule by exactly one declared negative-semantic fixture. The TT-4 cases that no on-disk fixture can express, an absent root idempotency key and an inconsistent method or policy pair, are derived in memory from the canonical presentations and run through the compiled schema by the validator.
trust_invariants.enforcement_boundary: Structural conformance is provable from these bytes. Every TX-* rule is a relying-party obligation that no schema, fixture, or validator in this repository can discharge; none of them is evidenced as implemented anywhere.

future_flip_actions.note: The actions a future, explicitly recorded Gate W2-I status flip would have to perform, in order. NONE of them is performed by this file, and listing them authorizes none of them.
actions: 1. Record the explicit Founder acceptance decision with evidence links in the status-flip commit (ADR-0001 D5). Acceptance is never inferred from a green validator or a green CI run.
2. Resolve every BLOCKING open item first — in particular the W2-F GET-token amendment — as its own reviewed change, before the flip commit.

3. Re-verify every digest in this delta against the on-disk bytes immediately before the flip: the four candidate members, the two accepted upstream pins, and the examples-manifest pin. A single stale pin voids the review the flip relies on.

4. Flip the successor member from PROPOSED to ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION and relabel the predecessor member SUPERSEDED-SUPPORTED in the ACCEPTED W2-D manifest, applying proposed_manifest_changes.adds_members with the re-verified digests. The flip is a whole-packet act: a half-flipped packet, where a member and its manifest disagree, is a consistency failure.
5. Leave the predecessor bytes untouched. Supersession relabels; it never edits, re-versions, or deletes the superseded document.
